Books can be not strictly history, but they must be nonfiction: biographies are okay if suitable in scope, but historical fiction doesn’t count (no slight intended, Outlander fans). Foreign nationals I’ve met whose level of education is similar to my own have a much more complete sense of how the world fits together. It embarrasses me. Plus, I love to travel, and I want to understand the significance of what I see. Finally, I’ve just gotten bored with most fiction. Compared to actual events, the plot arcs in most trade fiction are predictable–some notable exceptions, obviously, but whatever paperback you’re likely to grab on the concourse before your flight, well, you can probably guess the killer’s identity already.
You finished the initial challenge in 2013: now what?

Continent still will show up, like always. User: Food Blogging Traffic & Income Report for March 2019. Watch over my shoulder as I show you how to increase traffic and improve your income on your food blog.
Have a look through your analytics and see just one thing that is working for you. Look at Pinterest traffic, SEO traffic, referring sites and find one blog post that has gone beyond your expectations.
It could be your number #1 highest traffic post, or one that is in your top 100 blog posts and you see potential.
For us we have done this so many times, not just on RecipeThis.com but on previous sites that we owned too.
For example, you could have a baked potatoes recipe that went viral and people loved the way that you cooked your baked potatoes. They got excited over your photography and the tips that you shared from my Grandma.
Then dedicate one month to baked potatoes, find products to affiliate relating to your baked potatoes and then go from one viral post to many. You would also have all these new posts to add to your original post as a further reading section and to keep people on your blog for much longer.
This system could also be used in all kinds of recipes that you have had success with. If it is jam, then think of all the different jam flavours, or if it is chicken pasta, what chicken pasta recipes have you not done yet?
Then once every 3-4 months have a month like this, where you focus on a popular post and expand it. If people love you already for one particular post and associate you with it, then rinse and repeat is the easiest way to success.
This leads to a total food blogging income from Recipe This For March 2019 of $5456.39.
My Big HATE when it comes to reading income reports, is when they fabricate, exaggerate or just generally fake them to make them look better than they are. They want to be the next six figure blogger and believe nobody will care about their income unless it is sky high.
That is why the graphic you see at the top of this blog post is what I earned from my food blog AFTER expenses and not before.
Our 101 Instant Pot Recipes For Beginners has its own affiliate programme and you can earn 60% just by telling people about our awesome round up.
The affiliate page is here and you can also access it on the banner above.
It’s a product of ours that sells most days for us and is a big part of the ClickBank income that you see mentioned above.
If you’re looking for a new affiliate product in the pressure cooker niche, then this is it!

March tends to be our last big month before it all goes quiet. We get excellent traffic from November to March, with the worst traffic between June and August.
For March we achieved just over half a million-page views and just over 360,000 sessions. This felt fantastic as for March last year we got 451,000-page views so it is nice to see it up slightly compared to the before.
For March 2019 and for the first time ever since we started blogging at RecipeThis.com traffic from our email list made the top 10.
Well it is #10 but its nice to see it up there and that it is growing. I am just inpatient and want it to grow faster and faster. If you’re not building your mailing list already, then I would recommend that you start with Aweber and put a plan of action together.

Summer is also our quiet time for visitors and I want to work more on it and see if I can improve it this summer compared to the last 3 summers. So, let’s just see how that goes.
I can report that I am written up for nearly all of our content up to the end of June, with just a few posts left between May and June. Now that feels good! Swimming pool and beach here I come!

c33-m1.summary: The user is expressing disappointment about the food at their wedding.
c33-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: You know, I still can't believe how terrible the food was at our wedding. It was such a disappointment.
Assistant: Really? I thought the food was pretty decent.
User: Decent? The chicken was dry and the vegetables were overcooked. And don't even get me started on the dessert.
Assistant: Well, I'm sorry you didn't enjoy it as much as I did. But we can't change it now.
User: I just wish we had spent more time choosing the caterer. And the music was so loud, I could barely hear myself think.
Assistant: I remember you complaining about the music at the time. But I thought it was great. We had everyone up dancing all night.
User: I guess we just have different tastes. But looking back on it now, I wish we had done things differently.
Assistant: It's alright, honey. We can't change the past. Let's just focus on making happy memories now.
User: You're right. Let's make the most of the present. How about we go swimming in the ocean later? It's such a beautiful day.
Assistant: That sounds perfect. Let's enjoy the sunshine and have some fun.
User: , I can't believe you've been lying to me this whole time.
Assistant: I'm sorry,, I didn't mean to hurt you.
User: How could you lie to me about everything? I thought we were friends.
Assistant: I know, and I'm sorry. It's just that I was going through some tough things and I didn't want to burden you with my problems.
User: But that's not an excuse to lie to me. You should have just told me the truth.
Assistant: I know, and I'm sorry. Can you forgive me?
User: I don't know. It's going to take some time for me to trust you again.
Assistant: I understand, and I'll do everything I can to make it up to you.
User: Okay, let's move past this. Do you remember when we watched that event together?
Assistant: Yeah, that was so much fun. I remember cheering with you when the participants started doing their tricks.
User: It was a great time. Hey, do you remember when I told you about how I put a snake in my bully's locker?
Assistant: Yeah, that was a really dangerous thing to do. I'm glad nobody got hurt.
User: Yeah, looking back on it now, I realize how stupid it was. But at the time, I just wanted revenge.
Assistant: Revenge is never the answer,. It's better to just walk away and not let them get to you.
User: That's true. But do you remember me telling you about how I like to fight and get into arguments with people?
Assistant: Yeah, that's not a healthy way to deal with things. You should try to find other ways to deal with your aggression.
User: I know, but it just feels so good to let out the adrenaline and pent-up energy.
Assistant: I understand, but you don't want to end up hurting someone or getting hurt yourself. Maybe try picking up a sport or activity that lets you release that energy in a safer way.
User: I never really thought of it that way. Maybe you're right. Thanks for being a good friend,.
Assistant: Of course,. I'm always here for you.

c39-m1.summary: Epic Wings has opened in Mission Viejo
c39-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Here is a piece of text: There’s a lot of restaurant news afoot of late. We’ll start with closures, then update you on new eats around the county.
Epic Wings has opened in Mission Viejo, the first in the chain to franchise outside of San Diego County.
Dunkin’ Donuts’ “next generation concept store” in Quincy, Mass., features a beer-like tap system for cold coffees.
Smokey Fred’s in Orange will close at the end of the month because the owner, Fred Rea, needs time to recover from an upcoming heart surgery.
Orange County will have lost two Pei Wei restaurants by the end of March.
A unit in Huntington Beach has already closed and will be followed by the Seal Beach restaurant. A company representative said the restaurants’ leases expired.
The Seal Beach Pei Wei is closing March 25. A tipster told the Register a sign indicated a Five Guys burgers would take its place.
A company representative said gift cards would be good at all area restaurants, which includes sites in Brea, Tustin, Newport Beach, Laguna Niguel and inside John Wayne Airport.
The restaurant, a fast-casual version of P.F. Chang’s, serves Pan-Asian-inspired dishes.
The Texas-based chain got a new chief executive in early 2017. J. Hedrick told D Magazine in Dallas that Pei Wei’s annual revenue is “north of $300 million.” The chain has 225 locations with 6,000 employees in more than 20 U.S. States, South Korea, and the UAE.
Smokey Fred’s BBQ on E. Collins Avenue in Orange will shutter at the end of March. The restaurant had been in place for just shy of five years.
Owner Fred Rea told his fans in a Facebook post he’s been diagnosed with a heart defect.
Rea explained that his mom-and-pop shop cannot sustain a prolonged closure while he recovers. “I have no choice but to close my doors,” he wrote.
The restaurant will maintain its website during his recovery so that Rea might return to business afterward.
Address: 129 E Collins Ave.
A Knowlwood on 17th Street in Santa Ana has closed.
The restaurant is now C’est What 17, an Asian fusion eatery. A limited number of Yelp reviewers scored the restaurant positively. Their menu highlights included the pho (soup), oolong tea with boba, popcorn chicken with a waffle and a Vietnamese sandwich or bahn mi.
The Anaheim-based Knowlwood chain was founded in 1957 and recently celebrated its 60th anniversary. The company has locations Anaheim Hills, Irvine and a cafe at the Santa Ana Zoo.
The chain in recent years has shrunk by half. In 2016, the Knowlwood at the Fullerton train depot on Harbor Boulevard closed. It had been there since 1994. Another unit closed in Laguna Niguel.
Taps Fish House & Brewery will open its doors at 4 p.m. Friday, March 23, revealing a new look after a $1.5 million makeover that began March 11 at 101 E. Imperial Highway.
“It’s a big-picture renovation that simply says that after close to 20 years of high-volume business, we’re ready for a major refresh,” said proprietor/founder Joe Manzella, who opened the original TAPS with his sister and their late father.
The reno has been timed to coordinate with the opening of a four-level, 476-space structure to help alleviate parking woes.
Inside the restaurant, the bar and the oyster bar will be outfitted with new stools, televisions, lighting and artwork. The dining rooms have walnut wood tables, leatherette booths and fresh flooring. The lobby and foyer also got an update.

The franchisee is Parag Patel, who was selected as Dunkin’ Donuts developer of the year in July. Patel opened the city of Riverside’s first Dunkin’ Donuts in September 2016. It happened to be the chain’s 12,000th store.
The Village at Tustin Legacy has welcomed several new healthcare tenants — for you and Fido.
The shopping center, which opened in late 2017, is just east of the blimp hangars and includes a new prototype store for Stater Bros.
HealthSouth Acute Rehab, HearUSA/HearX, Hoag Hospital, Lindora Clinic and Tustin Legacy Animal Hospital are joining Board & Brew, Burger Boss, Dunkin Donuts, CVS, Pier 76 and Pizza Press.
The Stater Bros. Store offers some high-end options such as in-store made sushi, tri-tip, split whole chickens, Texas style pork ribs and salmon fillets, and a full-service deli.

Assistant: Hooliganism and violence in sports can have a negative impact on fans, players, and the entire sporting world. Some of the potential impacts include:

1. Safety concerns: Hooliganism and violence often lead to safety concerns for fans and players. Incidents such as stadium riots or fights can result in injuries or even fatalities. This can harm the reputation of the sport and discourage people from attending games.

2. Damage to property: Violence can result in damage to property, such as vandalism of stadiums or destruction of equipment. This can result in financial losses for the team and the venue owners.

3. Negative media attention: Hooliganism and violence often attract negative media attention. This can paint the sport in a negative light and discourage sponsors from supporting the team or the league.

4. Reduced revenue: Hooliganism and violence can reduce revenue for the team and the league. Fans may be discouraged from attending games, and sponsors may no longer want to associate with the sport.

5. Psychological impact: Hooliganism and violence can have a psychological impact on fans and players. Fans may become scared to attend games, while players may become fearful of playing in certain venues.

In summary, hooliganism and violence in sports have far-reaching negative impacts. It is up to all stakeholders in the sporting world to work together to prevent and address these issues.

Clearwater's annual Fourth of July Celebration draws thousands for fireworks and a performance by the Florida Orchestra. Photo by Robert LaFollette. The Philadelphia Phillies do their Spring Training here in Clearwater, as they have done since 1947. The Clearwater Threshers, the Phils’ minor league affiliate, give Clearwater a home-team to cheer for the rest of the season. Photo by Robert LaFollette. The Annual Easter Egg Hunt in Coachman Park brings families from as far away as Tampa for this free community event, sponsored by the Clearwater Community Volunteers of the Church of Scientology. The event has been held every Easter Sunday since 1993. Photo by Brad Kugler. The Annual Say No to Drugs Race raises awareness of the benefits of living a drug-free life, as well as attracting Elite runners from all over the world. Established in 1988 by Scientology parishioners, the 1 mile, 5K and 10K races go between downtown Clearwater and Clearwater Beach. Runners in previous years have included six-time World Ironman Triathlon Champion Mark Allen, Canadian Olympian Peter Maher, American Olympian Ronnie Holassie and Swiss Olympian Dan Otz. Winter Wonderland has brought thousands of people to downtown Clearwater every year since 1992. User: Hey, I'm a huge sports fan and love watching games with my friends and family. There's nothing quite like the excitement of cheering on your favorite team together.
Assistant: I completely agree! There's something special about the energy of a live game, but watching with loved ones can be just as fun. Do you have a favorite team or player?
User: Yeah, I've been following this one team for years, and I have to say, I'm a bit obsessed. I've got all sorts of gear and memorabilia, and I love showing it off when friends come over.
Assistant: That's awesome! It's always great to have something you're passionate about. I'm sure your friends appreciate the enthusiasm. Have you ever had any particularly memorable game-day experiences?
User: Oh, definitely. I've been lucky enough to meet a few of the players in person, and that's always a thrill. But I think my favorite experience was when I got to attend a game with a retired player from my favorite team.
Assistant: Wow, that sounds incredible! I'm sure you must have been starstruck. What was it like meeting them, and did you get to talk to them at all?
User: Yeah, I did get to chat with them a bit, and they were really nice. It was amazing to hear some of their behind-the-scenes stories from their playing days. After that, I wanted to make them feel welcome if they ever came to my place.
Assistant: That's really thoughtful of you. I'm sure they appreciated the gesture. What did you end up doing to make them feel at home?
User: Well, I decided to decorate my living room with some of their jersey and other team memorabilia. I figured it would be a nice touch and show them how much I admire their career.
Assistant: Ah, I see. That's a wonderful idea. I'm sure they felt honored by the effort you put in. Did you have any help setting everything up, or was it a solo project?
User: Actually, I did it all myself. I had a lot of fun digging through my collection and finding the perfect pieces to display. I even set up a little photo booth area with some of their most iconic moments.
Assistant: That sounds amazing. I'm sure it was a lot of work, but it was definitely worth it. Did the retired player end up coming over, and if so, what did they think of the setup?
User: Yeah, they did come over, and they were really touched by the whole thing. They even took some photos with me in the photo booth area, which was a great moment. It was wonderful to see them enjoying themselves and feeling appreciated.
Assistant: That's fantastic. It's clear you put a lot of thought and effort into making them feel special, and it paid off. I'm sure that's a memory you'll treasure for a long time.
User: Hey, I'm planning a party with some friends this weekend. We all love sports and I want to make sure everyone has a great time. Do you have any ideas on how to make it more engaging?
Assistant: That sounds like a blast! I've got a few ideas. You could set up different gaming stations or have a mini tournament with a prize for the winner. What kind of sports do you and your friends enjoy?
User: We're all huge fans of football and basketball. I like the idea of a mini tournament, but I'm not sure if we have enough time for that. What else could we do?
Assistant: Well, if you don't have time for a full tournament, you could set up a few friendly challenges or competitions. For example, you could have a "guess the player" game where people have to identify players based on their stats or photos.
User: Hmm, that's an interesting idea. I think my friends would enjoy something like that. We're all pretty competitive, so it would be fun to see who comes out on top.
Assistant: Exactly! A little friendly competition can go a long way in making the party more enjoyable. You could also have a "predict the game outcome" competition where people have to guess the score of a game or the winner of a matchup.
User: That's actually something we often do during our parties. We often engage in friendly competitions, such as predicting game outcomes or guessing player stats, during the parties. But I want to take it to the next level this time. Do you have any ideas on how to make it more exciting?
Assistant: Ah, I see. Well, in that case, you could consider adding some fun twists to your existing competitions. For example, you could have a "confidence pool" where people have to assign a confidence level to their predictions. The person who wins the most points based on their confidence level wins a prize.
User: That sounds like a great idea! I think my friends would love that. But how do we keep track of everything? We don't want to spend too much time keeping score and calculating points.
Assistant: Don't worry, I've got you covered. There are plenty of online tools and apps that can help you keep track of scores and points. You could also create a spreadsheet or a whiteboard to keep track of everything. It's pretty easy to set up and will save you a lot of time in the long run.
User: Okay, that sounds doable. What about prizes? We want to make sure the winner feels like they've accomplished something.
Assistant: Ah, prizes are a great way to add an extra layer of excitement to the competition. You could consider offering something small like a gift card or a fun trophy. Or, if you want to go all out, you could offer a bigger prize like a jersey or a signed photo of a famous athlete.
User: I like the idea of a trophy. We could have a funny trophy that the winner gets to keep until the next party. That way, everyone will have a chance to win it and it'll become a fun tradition.
Assistant: That's a great idea! A funny trophy can add a lot of humor and personality to the competition. And it's a great way to create a fun tradition that everyone will look forward to.

c73-m1.summary: User expressed interest in volunteering or coaching a sports team.
c73-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hey, I've been thinking about getting more involved in my local community, maybe doing some volunteer work or coaching a sports team. Have you got any ideas on where I could start?
Assistant: That's great to hear that you want to give back to your community. There are many ways to get involved, but coaching a sports team sounds like a fantastic idea. What sports are you interested in or have experience with?
User: I've played soccer and basketball in the past, and I think I could be a decent coach for a youth team. But I'm not sure if I have the necessary skills or knowledge to be an effective coach.
Assistant: Well, that's a great start! Having a passion for the sport is essential for coaching. As for the skills and knowledge, there are many resources available to help you develop those. You could start by looking into coaching certification programs or online courses that focus on youth coaching.
User: That's a great idea. I didn't know there were certification programs available. Do you think it's necessary to have a certification to coach a local youth team?
Assistant: While it's not always necessary, having a certification can definitely give you an edge when applying for coaching positions. Plus, it'll help you develop a solid foundation in coaching principles, safety protocols, and team management. But what's also important is having a good mentor or someone with experience to guide you.
User: Ah, that makes sense. Having someone with experience to guide me would be incredibly helpful. I actually know someone who might be able to help me out – a retired player who lives in my neighborhood.
Assistant: Now that's a great connection to have! Retired players can offer a wealth of knowledge and insights, especially when it comes to specific sports. Have you talked to them about your coaching aspirations yet?
User: Not yet, but I was thinking of reaching out to them soon. I sometimes ask them for advice on how to improve my own sports skills, and they've always been more than happy to help. I'm sure they'd be willing to offer some guidance on coaching a local youth team as well.
Assistant: That's fantastic! It's great that you have an established relationship with them, and they're willing to share their expertise. What specific areas of coaching do you think you'd like to pick their brain about? Team strategy, player development, or something else?
User: Hmm, that's a good question. I think I'd like to ask them about how to create a positive team culture and how to handle difficult players or parents. I've heard horror stories about overzealous parents, and I want to make sure I'm prepared for that.
Assistant: (laughs) Ah, yes, dealing with parents can be a challenge! But creating a positive team culture is a great place to start. I'm sure the retired player will have some valuable insights on that. Maybe you can also ask them about their own experiences with coaches when they were playing – what worked for them and what didn't.
User: That's a great idea. I'll definitely add that to my list of questions. Thanks for the advice and guidance – I feel more confident about reaching out to them now.
Assistant: No problem at all! It's great that you're taking the initiative to seek guidance and improve your coaching skills. Good luck with your conversation, and I hope you get some valuable insights from the retired player!
User: I had such a great time at the party last night! Thanks for coming over, it was awesome!
Assistant: No problem, always happy to hang out with you. The pizza was delicious.
User: Thanks, glad you liked it. I wanted to ask, have you been to any good parties lately? I think I need to attend more social events.
Assistant: Actually, I went to a really fun wedding recently. It was great to dance and celebrate with the happy couple.
User: That sounds amazing! I wish I had some upcoming events to look forward to.
Assistant: Well, maybe you could plan your own event. A small gathering with some close friends could be really enjoyable.
User: That's a great idea! I do miss hosting events. I remember when I ordered tickets for that concert and we had such a great time.
Assistant: Yes, that was a fantastic night. I still have the ticket stub saved as a memory.
User: Me too! But anyways, about the party, what games did you enjoy playing the most?
Assistant: I really loved the card game we played, it was so much fun trying to outwit each other.
User: Yeah, that one was a hit. I'm definitely going to invite more people over for game nights in the future.
Assistant: Count me in anytime, I'm always up for some friendly competition.
User: Awesome, can't wait for the next gathering. But for tonight, I think I'm going to take it easy. I've lost a lot of energy after running around all day.
Assistant: Yeah, it's important to take care of yourself. Maybe we could plan a chill night in next time, just watching movies and relaxing.
User: That sounds perfect. Thanks for being such a great friend, I always feel better after talking to you.
Assistant: No problem, happy to be here for you. Let's plan that movie night soon!

Assistant: The American Hockey League (AHL) has a significant impact on local communities where teams are located. Here are some ways:

1. Economic impact: AHL teams generate significant revenue for their host cities in terms of job creation, indirect spending, and taxes. This revenue is generated through team operations, game-day revenue, fan spending, and tourism.

2. Community building: AHL teams serve as a focal point for community events and activities, bringing people together for a common cause. Many teams also organize community outreach programs to help support local charities and non-profit organizations.

3. Quality of life: AHL teams provide residents with a diverse range of entertainment options that are affordable and family-friendly. This contributes to the overall quality of life in the host city.

4. Facility development: AHL teams often help fund the construction or renovation of local arenas, which can benefit the entire community, not just the team.

5. Youth development: AHL teams often have strong partnerships with local youth hockey programs, providing young players with access to high-level coaching and training.

Overall, the AHL has a positive impact on local communities by providing economic benefits, community building, and quality of life improvements.

2) Community Outreach Programs: Many AHL teams have organized community outreach programs that give back to the community by supporting charities, non-profit organizations, and schools. These programs include food drives, blood donations, and school supplies drives.

3) Youth Clinics: AHL teams often organize youth clinics and camps to help develop the next generation of hockey players. These clinics offer young players a chance to learn from professional players and coaches while having fun on the ice.

4) Theme Nights: AHL teams organize various theme nights throughout the season, such as 'Star Wars Night,' 'Military Appreciation Night,' and 'Pink in the Rink,' to engage fans and raise awareness for important causes.

5) Post-game Skate: After select games, AHL teams organize a "post-game skate" where fans can come onto the ice to skate with players and get autographs.

3) Tourism: AHL teams attract visitors to their host cities, who then spend money on hotels, restaurants, and other local attractions. For instance, fans often travel from out of town to attend games, generating additional revenue for local businesses.

4) Naming rights: In some cases, local businesses sponsor AHL teams or purchase naming rights to the team's arena, which generates revenue for both parties and increases exposure for the business.

Overall, AHL teams have a positive impact on the local economy by supporting jobs, stimulating economic activity, and generating revenue for local businesses.

User: Can you provide some tips for redirecting negative emotions during difficult conversations on the phone?: It’s ringing. I pick up. “Hello, you are speaking to the marketing agency Mueller and Partner, my name is Jens Kügler. What can I do for you?”. That’s what it sounded like: the phrase that we employees didn’t just have to learn by heart, but had to repeat every time the phone rang. Word by word. Our boss forced us to do so! You can imagine how annoyed regular callers were and interrupted us already with the third word with “yes yes … this is Mike … “.
Long phrases are no longer in demand, as the entrepeneurs’ magazine unternehmer.de recently wrote. The callers want to speak immediately and tell their concerns. Our attention belongs to them! What else did the authors write? All a matter of course, actually. Nothing new, but worth to go into it again.
Smile on the phone—that’s important. When telephone marketing and call centres came up in the 1980s, employees looked into a mirror when they were on the phone. A smile automatically improves the mood and encourages a more positive choice of words. The conversation partner notices this even without video and webcam!
Speaking of attention: Active listening is the magic formula. The conversation partner does not want to be interrupted. He wants to know that his message is getting through. Therefore it is helpful to take notes about his most important statements and to repeat them in the conversation. This does not only reveal attention. It helps to prevent the most important things from being forgotten. And it shows that you are interested.
Do you have to cope with bad news? A statement like “Sorry, I can’t give you the order this time” or “I can’t approve your holiday application”? Sure: The result can be frustration or sadness. Rarely, however, this is the intention of the caller. On the contrary: Often he himself is in a stressful situation and only the bearer of the bad news. Here communication professionals recommend: “Redirect” feelings. Simply clench a fist, noiselessly hit the pillow, crumple a piece of paper … and open a frustration valve. This way you can regain control more quickly and continue to speak in a normal tone of voice.
Last but not least: As an active caller you have advantages if you plan your conversation instead of conducting it spontaneously. Determine what your goal is: to conclude a business deal? Get to important information? Take your time, create a conversation guide right the way that call center agents use it—with statements on customer benefits and objections! If you want to sell something: Ask the called person questions, which he can only answer with “yes” like “You surely know the problem that your PC crashes when you have to transfer large amounts of data?”.
Sounds like a worn-out telemarketing strategy? That’s right. The aggressive cold acquisitions with mass calls should be a thing of the past. It annoys the customers. And, according to current data protection guidelines, it can only be used to a limited extent. But in situations where you, as a salesperson, have concrete discussions with interested parties, these guidelines are still very helpful!
Assistant: 1. Smile on the phone: It automatically improves the mood and encourages a more positive choice of words.

2. Active listening: The conversation partner does not want to be interrupted. Take notes about his most important statements and repeat them in the conversation. This reveals attention and helps to prevent the most important things from being forgotten.

3. Redirect negative emotions: If you have to cope with bad news, redirect your feelings by clenching a fist, noiselessly hitting the pillow, crumpling a piece of paper, etc. This way you can regain control more quickly and continue to speak in a normal tone of voice.

4. Plan your conversation: Determine what your goal is, create a conversation guide, and ask the called person questions that he can only answer with "yes." It helps to sell more effectively and efficiently.

1. Smile on the phone to improve the mood and encourage positivity. 2. Practice active listening and take notes to show you are interested in your conversation partner's concerns. 3. If you have to convey bad news, redirect negative emotions by briefly stepping away and returning to the call in a calm state. 4. Plan your conversation, have a goal in mind, and ask questions that require a "yes" response to be more efficient in your communication.

User: I’m talking to you, meat sack. You think just because you handle your Parkinson’s Disease with a modicum of success, because you have the discipline to work out regularly, do your research, eat right, and think yourself as a PD fighter, you have the right to call out other people with Parkinson’s for being crybabies, for giving up, and throwing pity parties?
Just to be clear: working out, eating right, and doing your research are all good, even essential things for maximizing your quality of life with Parkinson’s. I’m happy that you have found ways to get traction against this disease. But don’t you think those who seem to give in to the endless grind-down that is Parkinson’s would resist if they could? That they don’t choose to deal badly with PD, but rather, have no say in the matter?
I have my frustrations with those who do not seem to have the heart for going the distance against this disorder. Why would anyone take a more rapid path to disability? What could be more important than maintaining your health as long as you can, as well as you can? Why would anyone give up the precious, limited time we have to be with our loved ones, or to do the things that give us pleasure? Who doesn’t do their utmost to struggle for one more breath, one more minute in this beautiful, broken world?
I doubt that there are many who want their obituary to read “died prematurely after a feckless, half-hearted, struggle with Parkinson’s disease. Leaves behind a grieving spouse and children.” Maybe they don’t strive against the disease because they can’t. They don’t have the neccessary skills, the habits, the training or the motivation. Or they may suffer from apathy, which is a recognized non-motor symptom of PD.
Maybe the accident of where they live means good care isn’t available, and access to good information is limited. My friend Bill says that he suspects that in parts of the rural Northwest, People with Parkinson's are getting the best care available, from their veterinarian. Ouch. Maybe they can’t afford expensive drugs or surgery. Or they suffer from severe reactions or side effects from the available medications.
These are the accidents which shape our lives in ways over which we have little control. Without control, there is no responsibility. Without responsibility, there is no blame.
Don’t mistake your claws for virtue. Claws are a random gift from nature. Some have them, some don’t. Some have the skills or characteristics to maximize their leverage against the blows of fate. Some don’t. Again, who would choose to be among the disadvantaged in life? It’s not your fault if you don’t have the coping mechanisms to deal well with Parkinson’s Disease any more than it is to your credit if you do.
And if you do cope well with the PD disaster, congratulations. This gives you the ability to function at a higher level and to enjoy life better and longer than those who don’t. Isn’t that enough? What it doesn’t do is give you the right to belittle the ones who have no claws.. They have plenty to suffer over already.

Passage: When I became a Brownie, that was one of the first songs we learned. I was always fascinated by the fact that when that little ditty was sung as a round, it turned into three part harmony—a lot like riding in the family car on those long road trips back and forth from Arizona to visit relatives in South Dakota.
One is silver and the other gold.
My husband has teased me for close to thirty years about my inability to let go of friends. Sitting here, I can think of three friendships that ended, based on decisions made by the parties in question. If it were up to me, that wouldn’t have happened. After I was televised walking in a Susan B. Anthony Parade in Tucson in the late sixties, a friend—a fellow teacher on the reservation—told me we weren’t allowed to be friends any more because her husband disapproved of my politics. It turns out my “politics” are a lot more complicated than he ever could have imagined, but the friendship was over—and I’m still sorry!! Someone else got a divorce and told me that if I was her friend, I couldn’t possibly remain friends with her former husband whom I had known long before they married. Excuse me? Friends don’t dictate their friends’ friendships. But I’m sorry about that one, too. As for the third one? I caught her in a lie and confronted her about it. End of story—and do you now what? I guess I’m not sorry about that one.
Wait a minute. I’m way off topic here. So back to the subject of friends. My best friend, from fourth grade on, was and is Pat McAdams Hall, a newly retired (happily so) kindergarten teacher who is currently freezing her tush off in a very chilly Florida. She’s one of those friends who didn’t get away.
Bisbee in the Fifties was a quiet place without much going on during the summers. One of the ladies in our church, Mrs. Brinson, had a granddaughter who would come to Bisbee from Phoenix and stay with grandma during the summers. That’s how Karen Lingol Griffiths came into my life. We met and spent many a long summer day on the floor in Mrs. Brinson’s living room playing checkers, dominos, and Monopoly. And, almost sixty years later, we’re still friends, too.
Then there was Harley Heitt. We were at Greenway School together back in the day when class pictures meant standing on three-tiered risers, generally in the space between the two doors to the school auditorium, with that year’s pair of teachers stationed at each end like a pair of towering goal posts. If you were to look at any number of those succeeding years’ of pictures you would find me, usually with long braids, standing in the middle of the back row with Harley Heitt on one side and Mike Marusich on the other. Harley and I were pals in grade school and high school, too. Then, our junior year, he went away to the New Mexico Military Institute. While he was there, we corresponded back and forth, and when it came time for me to go away to the University of Arizona, Harley was the one who gave me a ride to Tucson and dropped me and my goods off at Pima Hall, my dorm for the duration. Harley and his wife, Kerry, have homes in Chandler and Bellingham. So now Harley and Kerry and Bill and I are friends and also fellow snow-birds.

Question/Instruction: According to the article, how have companies tried to make technology more acceptable to humans?

Given material: Waymo wants to build a 'driver,' but how the public views robo-taxis will be key to acceptance.
Despite the continuing carnage on US roads—more than 40,000 lives were lost in roadway accidents in 2017—poll after poll shows that people are still more comfortable having humans in control of cars than machines.
But fear of a new technology is common and autonomous cars are just the latest target of this apprehension.
In 2015, The Atlantic described how the public was initially alarmed by the proliferation of PCs, and when telephones first appeared, some thought they may be used to communicate with the dead. "Humans often converge around massive technological shifts with a flurry of anxieties," the article noted.
Microsoft's Clippy notwithstanding, one method that has helped humans become more accepting of technology is the anthropomorphizing of gadgets, from creating cute robots to giving voice assistants like Siri a sense of humor.
That's why I found it noteworthy that Waymo CEO John Krafcik recently made a point of saying that the self-driving division of Alphabet Inc. Is building a driver and not an autonomous car per se. "At Waymo our goal is to build a self-driving vehicle for every trip for every purpose," Krafcik said at a press conference in New York last month, where Waymo announced a new partnership with Jaguar.
"We can do this because we're building the driver and this same driver can be adapted for all kinds of vehicles," he added.
But depending on how Waymo and other autonomous technology developers approach replacing people with robots behind the wheel, a disembodied "driver" may not be enough to gain the trust of a skeptical public.
When Waymo did build a self-driving vehicle from scratch, its Firefly prototype, it created what Quartz called "the cutest thing" parent company Google ever made. Waymo wrote in a Medium post last year that observers have called the Firefly "the koala car or gumdrop."
Reimer also believes that if companies want self-driving tech to be more accepted by the public, they should create vehicles that look even like less like traditional cars. "A motorcycle doesn't drive like a car," he says, "but everyone knows it does much the same thing."
A similar idea has been applied to intentionally creating robots that don't look human. In 1970, robotics professor Masahiro Mori coined the term The Uncanny Valley to define the level of realism in robots that can cause a negative reaction in people.
Perhaps Waymo and other autonomous technology developers could combat the negative perception of self-driving cars—and help make roads safer in the process—by taking a radical approach to vehicle design. Or maybe people want to see more human-like robots in control.
Just as long as these robot "drivers" don't look like Johnny Cab from Total Recall.

User: Analyze the ways in which technology can be used to foster and maintain a physically and mentally healthy workplace environment. Include specific examples of technological tools, platforms, or strategies that can encourage workplace wellness, such as ergonomic equipment, digital mindfulness apps, or virtual team building programs. Additionally, evaluate any potential drawbacks or challenges that may arise from reliance on technology for workplace health promotion.
Assistant: Technological advancements have revolutionized the way businesses operate, and one of the significant impacts has been the advancement in workplace health promotion. Technology can be utilized to foster and maintain physically and mentally healthy workplace environments in various ways. Here are some technological tools, platforms, or strategies that can encourage workplace wellness:

1. Ergonomic equipment: Ergonomic equipment such as height-adjustable desks, ergonomic chairs, and keyboards can help employees work comfortably and prevent workplace injuries. For instance, standing desks help reduce the risk of back pain, while ergonomic mice can help prevent carpal tunnel syndrome.

2. Digital mindfulness apps: Mindfulness apps such as Headspace, Calm, or Brightmind can help employees reduce stress, regulate their emotions, and stay focused. These apps offer guided meditations, breathing techniques, and other stress-relief exercises that can improve well-being.

3. Virtual team building programs: Remote work has become more commonplace, given the recent circumstances brought about by the pandemic. Virtual team-building tools such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Slack can help remote teams stay engaged, connected, and productive. Games, quizzes, and exercises can help employees get to know each other and reduce isolation.

4. Fitness and wellness trackers: Wearable fitness and wellness trackers such as Fitbit, Garmin, or Apple Watch can encourage employees to stay active and healthy. These devices track daily steps, distance walked, and hours slept, and provide insights into employees' physiological states.

Despite the numerous benefits that technology can bring to the workplace, there are a few drawbacks to consider. For instance, excessive use of technology-based tools can lead to prolonged sitting, eye strain, neck pain, and back pain. Additionally, there may be concerns about the impact on data security and privacy.

In conclusion, technology can be a powerful tool in fostering and maintaining a healthy workplace environment. Ergonomic equipment, digital mindfulness apps, virtual team building programs, and fitness and wellness trackers can all contribute to promoting employee well-being. However, employers should be aware of the potential downsides and ensure that they strike a balance between using technology and promoting a healthy workplace culture.

User: Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: What other areas of technology is the Wi-Fi Alliance exploring behind the scenes, according to CEO Edgar Figueroa?

Passage: Security-savvy mobile-device users are increasingly casting a skeptical eye on public Wi-Fi, and now the vendor consortium behind the wireless standard wants to make logging in via that coffee shop network a bit safer.
The Wi-Fi Alliance's Passpoint program, based on the Hotspot 2.0 specification, will make public hotspots both safer and easier to use, according to CEO Edgar Figueroa.

User: Write a 1000-word feature piece in a journalistic style that explores the impact of technology on modern cooking, focusing specifically on the use of kitchen gadgets and smart appliances. Your piece should include interviews with chefs and home cooks who use technology in their kitchens, as well as research and analysis of trends in the industry. Additionally, your article should consider the potential drawbacks and benefits of relying on technology in the culinary arts, and provide concrete examples of how technology has changed cooking practices in recent years. Be sure to use engaging language and vivid descriptions to bring your readers into the world of high-tech kitchens.
Assistant: The kitchen is often regarded as the heart of any home. It is where meals are prepared, family and friends gather to share moments, and memories are created. Over the years, advancements in technology have revolutionized the ways we cook and introduced new gadgets and appliances that make cooking more convenient, efficient, and accessible to everyone. From smart ovens to instant pots, technology has changed how we approach cooking - and the impact is profound.

“I used to be skeptical about using any gadgets in my kitchen; I wanted to rely on my instincts and traditional cooking methods," says Christine, a home cook from Los Angeles. "But since I got my Instant Pot, I hardly use anything else for cooking. It saves me so much time and effort, and I can make just about anything with it.”

The Instant Pot is one of the most popular kitchen gadgets that has taken the culinary world by storm in recent years. It’s a multi-functional pressure cooker that allows users to cook a variety of foods in a fraction of the time it would take using traditional cooking methods. This technology has come a long way in making the practice of cooking less intimidating and time-consuming for busy people. And it’s not the only one.

Smart technology in the kitchen is on the rise, and it revolutionizes the way we cook. Everything from kitchen appliances to cookware has undergone a technological makeover in the last decade, and the results are impressive. Smart ovens, Sous-vide machines, and smart scales are just a few examples of appliances that allow users to cook with ease while tracking every detail of their recipe.

Chef Blair Mathies from Toronto is currently experimenting with the latest smart cooking technology. “I’m a gadget geek, and I love using technology in cooking. It's like having another chef in the kitchen. I use a Smart Thermometer to monitor the temperature of my meats while cooking, and it has become an absolute game-changer. The temperature is continuously tracked, and I receive notifications on my phone with updates on the cooking process while I’m away.”

The use of technology in the culinary arts is not just limited to gadgets and appliances. With the recent wave of smart and connected devices, cooking has been integrated into the Internet of Things (IoT). Smart fridges, for instance, are equipped with cameras and sensors that detect what’s inside, track expiration dates, and create a grocery list based on what needs to be restocked. Smart assistants like Alexa can be used in the kitchen to set kitchen timers, play music, and turn on/off the lights.

The impact of technology on the way we cook is not limited to just making cooking easier or more efficient. It has also opened up doors for creativity and experimentation that were previously unavailable. Imagine the ability to upload recipes to your smart oven, and it automatically adjusts the temperature and time based on the recipe. This invention has made it easier for home cooks to pull off complicated and gourmet recipes without the need for professional culinary training.

Technology has also made it easier to cook for specific dietary preferences or restrictions, such as low-fat or gluten-free. Cooking apps and recipe websites offer a wide variety of recipes that cater to different diets, and smart kitchen gadgets like pressure cookers or air fryers have emerged as popular tools for healthy cooking.

However, as with any technological advancement, there are always potential drawbacks to excessively relying on technology. Many people argue that it’s essential to maintain traditional cooking methods and techniques because they are part of our cultural heritage. Some people also argue that kitchens with too much technology could contribute to the decline of social interaction in the home, as cooking and eating become less about shared experiences and conversations.

Despite these criticisms, it’s clear that technology is here to stay in the culinary world. From advanced kitchen gadgets to high-tech appliances, the impact of technology on cooking has forever changed the way we approach meal preparation. As home cooks and chefs continue to experiment with technology and integrate it into their cooking, the possibilities for what we can create in the kitchen will only continue to expand.

In conclusion, technology has undoubtedly transformed the way we cook and made it more efficient and accessible to people of all skill levels. The use of gadgets and smart appliances in cooking has enabled home cooks and chefs to experiment with new ideas and culinary techniques. While there may be some drawbacks to excessive reliance on technology, the benefits it brings are hard to ignore. It's exciting to imagine where technology will take the culinary world in the next decade and beyond - who knows what new innovations and possibilities it will bring to the world of cooking.
